Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

ple · generated: PLE’s co-authored route starts from engineers’ structured seed briefs, uses Creator and Solver agents to construct and challenge environments and graders, and ends with expert validation and difficulty intensification.

candidate.third11.ple.coauthoring.v2

  • The solver is isolated from graders and references; the described loop tests mean performance across typically three attempts rather than assuming a task is hard after one failure.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

ple · evaluates: PLE’s documented evaluation gives an agent the instruction and environment without rubric, grader or reference access, then grades collected deliverables outside the agent container; model/harness pairs run every task three times with a six-hour agent budget.

candidate.third11.ple.evaluation-separation.v2

  • Infrastructure failures are rerun, while runs ending without a gradable deliverable score zero. Results are scoped to the model plus harness and cannot be interpreted as real engineering sign-off.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

ple · human annotation: For PLE’s expert-authored route, practising engineers write a realistic work request, construct a multi-format project environment and specify weighted evidence-bound rubric checks on the deliverable; the paper reports 941 rubric items across 44 tasks.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

ple · evaluates: PLE’s v2 paper grades expert-authored tasks by weighted binary rubrics and most co-authored deliverables by 0.4 times constraint compliance plus 0.6 times a hard-constraint-gated normalized objective score.

candidate.third11.ple.hybrid-grading.v2

  • Twelve co-authored graders also use LLM judgments for narrative soft constraints; two site-design and two MEP-coordination tasks retain their own scores. The hybrid formula is not universal to all 85 tasks.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

ple · access terms: The PLE repository describes 29 public development tasks behind a Hugging Face terms gate and 56 hidden test tasks; it declares Apache 2.0 for the project, while the paper states that environments contain no client-confidential material and use generated or redistributable source files.
